title: Affine lifting of a map from a perfect complex
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U be a quasi-compact open, let E' be an object of D_QCoh(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], and let A be a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-perfect-complex]. For every morphism \alpha:A|_U\to E'|_U, there exist a perfect object A' of D(\mathcal O_X), a morphism \beta:A'\to A that is an isomorphism on U, and a morphism \gamma:A'\to E' such that \alpha=\gamma|_U\circ(\beta|_U)^{-1}; moreover A'=A\otimes^L I for some perfect object I of D(\mathcal O_X), with \beta induced by a morphism I\to\mathcal O_X. In particular, if A is supported on a closed subset T, then A' is supported on T.

proof.text: Take a representative G of A under Q, and apply the K-flat resolution theorem to obtain P → G. Its quasi-isomorphism and the canonical representative isomorphism give e_A:Q(P) ≅ A.

Apply the Koszul tensor-roof construction to this fixed P, the open morphism alpha, and e_A. Obtain J, its chain augmentation u, gamma, and the restriction isomorphism b_U satisfying the two equations. Define I=Q(J), A'=Q(Tot(P tensor J)), and beta by the explicit augmentation formula. The witnesses P,J,e_A and reflexive model isomorphisms prove IsDerivedTensorAugmentation directly.
Apply perfect_derivedTensor to A,I and their K-flat representatives P,J, using e_A and the identity isomorphism of Q(J). This proves A' perfect.

For any closed support T and x outside T, apply the pointwise tensor stalk vanishing theorem with the given cohomology stalks of A. It proves every cohomology stalk of A' vanishes. This argument needs no claim that stalkwise vanishing implies vanishing on a neighbourhood.
